title: A Treatise on Vampires
subtitle: Supplemental Documentation on Vampires and Vampirism

blocks.text: Deciding that near immortality was not enough, a Dark Elf Necromancer named Dhakrik Yulzic sought to perform a ritual to obtain True Immortality, like his Dark Fae father. In the Year 100 of the Sun, at approximately the same time that Dwarves, Ogres and other “lesser species” were entering the world, Dhakrik attempted to bind his soul to his body forever. Though Zoggakomen loves all the children that pass into The World Beyond, the God of Death was filled with rage that one being would attempt to deny him of that eternal embrace. It is a rare thing for a god to appear on the mortal plane, but his wrath would be administered in person; Zoggakomen granted Dhakrik his wish— True Immortality—but with a price so terrible that it sent the young necromancer into an abyss of despair. First, the curse tore away his bond to the Onyx Stone and prevented him from ever forming another, prohibiting him from ever performing true magic again. Furthermore, not only was he banished from the desert he so loved but also the sun itself would now forever be his enemy; its warm rays burned his flesh and obliterated him, forcing him to endure a full century in agony as his body regenerated.

When he recovered, he found himself in a dark crypt, covered in the strange writing of the people of the island nation to the southwest, the Obedotish. Not only would he have to learn this strange new culture, but he would have to learn exactly what he had become and why he had this overwhelming thirst that could not be quenched by the water from an underground spring. He dared to venture above ground at night and when he happened across the first villager, he discovered the source of his polydipsia. In a blur of speed he didn’t realize he possessed, Dhakrik leapt at the man and sank long fangs into his throat. In under a minute he had drained his first victim dry, the body white from the loss of blood. This is his curse and the curse of anyone so infected by his tainted blood.

There are many stories, legends if you will, of the creatures of the dark, the children and followers of the Raven Spirit, considered one of the Great Spirits in Obedotish. Some of which I will narrate for your knowledge and prudence, lest you encounter one of them.

Legend has it that a small town in the Chiefdom of 𝔇𝘶𝘱𝘢𝘳𝘨𝘳𝘢𝘷𝘦, some people began to feel the calling of the Raven Spirit, the one to defy the nature of all Guardian Spirits, the one tasked to lead the souls of the deceased to their next path. This Spirit is now more commonly known in the land of the living as Dhakrik Yulzic, be it the darkness the name entails or the horrors he has committed, the name is not spoken lightly. The Raven Spirit corrupted from the inside, it is still not clear if this was an early effect of the incoming Umbraeth and Lumivoras that would soon populate Onyxia or if it would be the darkness hidden by the Spirit unhappy with its place in the order of things. Those who followed him were granted outstanding abilities in death, such as turning into gusts of wind that sucked the souls of the living or extracted their lifeforce channeling it to the Raven Spirit to increase his power and might and that of his loyal followers.

Many other legends have spread throughout the years, centuries, such as that pertaining a renown sorceress called Nahualli, known in Obedotish as the enchantress due to her outstanding qualities and beauty and the power of the magic language she used, old as time itself, she is said to have been the very first ‘witch’ of the wilderness cursed by the Raven Spirit to become his servant, the curse took hold of her and destroyed her from the inside as, in order to survive, she had to feed on children, or so the stories go, and

the first victims were her own. Now she roams the lands lamenting alongside all other Nahualli witches with deep hatred for Dhakrik Yulzic and all his brethren. The resentment and hatred is such that in some forests of Obedotish, now also spreading to other areas of Onyxia, whenever there is a lamenting Nahualli moving about the darkness and negative emotions found in the forest can drive a living person mad, most avoid forests where these beings have been spotted at night, and most are mainly protective of the children, for many have fallen victim of these harpies and their schemes.

The Tlilcuahuitl, or legend of the dark tree, originated in a small village in 𝔏𝘢𝘮𝘭𝘢𝘮, where a man that had never been seen before moved in claiming to want to start a new life in the Obedotish Dynasty, since he never caused any problems, people did not oppose a man from the Shido Empire called Takeo to live among them. He was said to have bought a ranch with hopes of settling in and making friends. However, something wasn't right and no one liked him. Soon after he arrived, townsfolk began noticing their animals were dying and all were found to have their blood drained. One night, some of them decided to investigate what was doing this and were hunting at night. Much to their surprise, they found Takeo, biting at the neck of an animal. Full of shock they tried to chase him away, but he was too fast and got away. They didn't know what to do, until an old sorceress told them to surround his ranch, set it ablaze with some talismans granted by Spirit Shamans and stab him through the heart with a stake of a black walnut tree. As he was being stabbed, Takeo cried out that he would return one day and get his revenge. For no one truly knew that these dark beings were immortal and would not be utterly destroyed. He was buried far away from the resting place of all inhabitants in Obedotish, but something strange began occurring over his tomb. A tree began to grow and the townspeople began to believe that the day the tree grew too much and tore, would be the day Takeo would return for his revenge.

There is also a legend from the capital of 𝔄𝘵𝘭𝘪𝘻𝘰𝘤, where during times of war between tribes and clans before the shaky unification of the diverse Obedotish Dynasty, during which it was perfectly normal for people to see piles of dead bodies in the streets. However, it was not normal for these bodies to have two holes in their necks and have all their blood gone. Surprised and shocked by the bodies they found, two generals asked their troops to investigate the nearby houses for anything suspicious. Sure enough, one troop of soldiers found a house with an insane amount of jars, full of blood. They were tasked with staking the house and they summoned Spirit Shamans to purify the houses of those affected so that they could continue on with their next path after death. Just when they thought no one was going to come to the house that had been surrounded by soldiers, they felt bloodlust and malice all around them, causing some of them to freeze in fear. They watched as this figure looked like a man and walked up to the house. The general ordered his troops to attack, ensuring the archers shot behind the warriors who took their spears and swords and, although they were terrified, they did just that. The man fell, sprawled right in front of his door and when the soldiers approached, he said with mock sarcasm and resignation, “there’s more of us and they will come for all of you”. The soldiers were frozen in fear, but the general walked up to the man, pointed his spear at the man’s heart and finished him off. Though they had killed this man, bodies with holes and void of blood continued to show up. To this day, it is said these beings not only reside in Obetodish still, but they have spread across the whole of Onyxia.
While the actual attributes of a vampire can vary based on the species of the individual being “Turned,” they share the following common characteristics.

blocks.label: Undeath
blocks.text: While vampires are considered True Immortals, this is only because they are already technically dead. They have no heartbeat and their bodies are typically the same temperature as the ambient atmosphere. They do not sweat or produce excrement, though they do salivate and blood flows through their veins by magical means. Their muscles are also powered by the curse itself and not as a result of blood within them.

blocks.label: Retractable Fangs
blocks.text: Vampires can extend the length of their canine teeth into prodigious hollow fangs which are sharp enough to puncture even the thickest animal hides. These fangs serve as siphons to drink the blood from their prey, usually through the neck. Occasionally, when a vampire is excessively thirsty, enraged or experiencing other strong emotions, their fangs may extend of their own accord.

blocks.label: Retractable Claws
blocks.text: Useful for melee attacks against armed prey, vampires may extend their natural fingernails into claws, the length of which can be fully controlled from simply long fingernails to fingers that morph into claws that are as long as short swords. These claws are razor sharp, may be serrated and as strong as steel.

blocks.label: Dynamic Irises
blocks.text: Though all vampires can change their eye colour at will, sometimes strong emotions or thirst may cause them to change on their own. Older vampires are able to control them much better, but even they occasionally lose that ability if overwhelmed with thirst.

blocks.label: Infertility
blocks.text: All vampires are sterile and cannot have offspring through natural procreation. The only way to generate more vampires is through the process of “Turning.”

blocks.label: Food and Drink
blocks.text: Normal food and drink can be consumed, but it has no flavour and provides no nutritional value for a vampire. Alcohol and narcotics do not affect them. However, vampires cannot digest or process anything eaten or drank and therefore must expel it by vomiting.
Though vampirism is a curse, it is not without its advantages. These are listed below by their original Obedotish names as well as what they are called in Onyxian Common Tongue.

blocks.label: Chiqap Mana Wañuq (The True Immortal)
blocks.text: Vampires cannot truly die. Like Fae, even if their physical form is completely destroyed, they will regenerate, it will just take time.

blocks.label: Edadpa Kallpan (The Strength of Age)
blocks.text: Vampires gain power as they age, increasing all of their abilities to the maximums described below.

blocks.label: Kurku allichay (Body Repair)
blocks.text: Vampires can heal ordinary wounds in seconds, critical wounds in minutes and mortal wounds in hours. Severed limbs can regenerate in a few days or weeks. Complete regeneration of the entire body can take a full century. Regeneration is amplified by the consumption or application of blood and weakened if blood deprived.

blocks.label: Rikchay Tikraq (Shape Changer)
blocks.text: Due to their roots in Obedotish, vampires have the ability to turn into other animals and creatures of similar size, or multiple creatures of smaller size. For example, a vampire can turn into a wolf or a flock of ravens. In that form, they have the abilities of those creatures only, but retain their own intelligence. When transforming into a group of animals, any animals killed apply damage to the vampire when it returns to its original shape.

blocks.label: Musquy Puriy (Dream Walking)
blocks.text: Their powerful psychic abilities give Vampires the ability to enter the dreams of another and influence them. The distance of this effect and the amount of control over the dreams is proportional to the age and power of the individual vampire and the willpower of the individual they are trying to influence.

blocks.label: Esclavoman Tukuchiy (Enslavement)
blocks.text: Through a combination of a seductive trance and keeping a victim partially drained of blood, a vampire may create a slave or thrall that is subject to their will. Older vampires have the ability to command a dozen individuals and these often guard them during daylight or carry out mundane tasks.

blocks.label: Kallpawan Agilidadwan (Strength and Agility)
blocks.text: Vampires are much stronger than their base species and with much faster reflexes. Though this is not reflected by muscle mass, they can be as strong as up to twenty members of their species and move so fast that they are imperceptible to the average eye. Their speed comes in bursts and cannot be maintained for long distance travel.

blocks.label: Huk Cazadorpa Sentidonkuna (The Senses of a Hunter)
blocks.text: All of a vampire's ordinary senses are enhanced, but above all they have the uncanny ability to sense prey up to fifty feet away by their heartbeat. Though the detection is auditory, the vampire “sees” the sound in his vision, even through obstacles.
At its very heart, vampirism is a transmittable curse and comes with many distinct disadvantages. As with strengths, these are first listed by their Obedotish names.

blocks.label: Yawar Ch'akiy (Blood Thirst)
blocks.text: Vampires must feed on at least a pint of blood from a sentient being per week or their powers begin to weaken. The longer they go without blood the more thirsty for blood they become. They also begin to show physical signs of rapid aging. If they go for longer than one month without blood they fall into a deep trance. The presence of a warm blooded creature will immediately awaken them and force them to gorge themselves on blood. Once fed or after resuming regular feedings, the vampire's powers become fully restored. Some vampires abstain from taking blood from sentient beings, though substitution requires more frequent feedings and never offers a vampire the full extent of their powers.

blocks.label: Tutapi Kawsak (Creature of the Night)
blocks.text: Sunlight in any form can destroy a vampire's body, turning the exposed flesh to ash and forcing regeneration. Full exposure will disintegrate a vampire and they will need to completely regenerate.

blocks.label: Cripta Puñuy (Crypt Sleep)
blocks.text: Vampires must reside in a prepared crypt or coffin during their sleep. They may not move out of this coffin between full sunrise and full sunset.

blocks.label: Qullqi (Silver)
blocks.text: Silver is nearly as dangerous as sunlight, scorching any flesh that touches it with painful blisters. Staking a vampire through the heart or cutting off its head with a silver blade can result in disintegration.

blocks.label: Tuta Llantuy (Nightshade)
blocks.text: Depending upon the dosage received by ingestion or directly introducing it into the bloodstream, nightshade or poison derived from it can cause sickness or paralysis. A sufficient dose can force a vampire into a deep trance identical to one they would experience from lack of blood.

blocks.label: Espejokuna (Mirrors)
blocks.text: A vampire's physical form is not reflected in a mirror, yet its clothing will be visible.

blocks.label: Llantuykuna (Shadow)
blocks.text: Vampires do not throw a shadow, in any form of light.

blocks.label: Mana Magiayuq (Without Magic)
blocks.text: Other than their innate vampiric abilities, vampires cannot use magic, including waystones. If a mage is turned, they lose all their magical abilities.
As stated above, vampires must feed (ideally on sentient beings) in order to avoid rapid aging and deep hibernation, however being bitten by a vampire is not without consequences for the victim.

blocks.label: Feeding
blocks.text: Being fed upon by a vampire is physically draining as there is a psychological effect as in addition to the loss of blood. Victims are considered wounded for 24 hours following a feeding, unless treated by a healer.

blocks.label: Draining
blocks.text: Completely draining a victim of their blood always leads to death.

blocks.label: Turning
blocks.text: Turning is the only way for a vampire to propagate the species and there are three ways to pass vampirism to another being.

blocks.label: Consecutive Feedings
blocks.text: Normal feedings require one pint of blood and there is a 5% chance of passing the curse with a single bite. However, consecutive feedings on the same victim or even if a victim is fed upon on separate occasions by a different vampire can dramatically increase the likelihood of turning, but 5% per feeding until turning becomes a certainty.

This is expressed in the game by having the victim roll 1d20 each time they are fed upon (or the vampire can roll if the victim is an NPC). For the first feeding, the roll must exceed a 1 and each additional feeding adds 1 to the difficulty until it becomes 20 and the victim automatically turns.

blocks.label: Drastic Feeding
blocks.text: Draining a victim of half its blood in one feeding has a 10% chance of passing vampirism to them.
For the game mechanics, see the Enthrall Chart below.
If the victim recovers per the chart, subsequent feedings increase the difficulty by 5%, starting at 15% (3 on 1d20) with the first following feeding.

blocks.label: Transfusion
blocks.text: Completely draining a victim of blood and then forcing them to drink the vampire’s own tainted blood always results in passing vampirism to the victim. This is usually done by the vampire cutting a gash on their chest or wrists.

blocks.label: Enthralling
blocks.text: As stated above, a vampire is able to take a sentient being as their thrall and the older the vampire, the more thralls they may command.

blocks.label: Drastic Feeding
blocks.text: The process of enthralling a victim includes a seductive trance and the draining of half of the victim’s blood. There are, however, multiple possible outcomes of the enthralling process that are beyond the vampire’s control. The greatest chance is, of course, the enthrallment of the victim, but there is also a substantial chance that the victim may die and a small chance of either turning the victim or their full recovery.
Consult the following chart for the percentage as well as the roll spread on 1d20 that determines the result. Enthrall Chart Result Chance Roll
Turned 10% 1-2
Enthrallment 50% 3-12
Full Recovery 10% 19-20
